name: Bazel
summary: A multi-language build system that analyzes declared targets into an action graph, executes actions in controlled environments, and reuses results through incremental and remote caching.

features.name: Declared target and action graph
features.description: Bazel's official documentation describes analysis of packages and targets into an action graph, where actions and their inputs determine the work needed to produce build outputs.
benefits: Makes dependencies and build work available for parallel scheduling and querying
Separates declarative target descriptions from execution of individual actions
costs: Rule analysis and configuration add a substantial conceptual layer
Incorrect or incomplete dependency declarations can invalidate incremental results

features.name: Hermetic sandboxed actions
features.description: The official documentation states that Bazel uses sandboxes to restrict action visibility and support hermetic execution, while its hermeticity guidance ties reproducibility to declared inputs and controlled environments.
benefits: Reduces accidental dependence on undeclared host files and tools
Provides a basis for reproducible local or remote action execution
costs: Actions that rely on undeclared host state can fail or require explicit escape hatches
Sandbox setup and platform constraints can add execution overhead

features.name: Content-addressed build caching
features.description: Bazel documents caching action results and dependency graph state across builds, including remote caching, so unchanged inputs and command configuration can avoid repeating eligible work.
benefits: Speeds repeated and distributed builds by reusing prior action results
Combines dependency analysis with incremental rebuild decisions
costs: Cache correctness depends on complete input, toolchain, and environment keys
Remote cache availability and trust add operational dependencies

mathematical_views.question: When does a configured target set admit a valid action execution order and a set of required inputs?
assumptions: Targets and generated actions are vertices with directed dependency edges
Configuration and toolchain selection are held fixed for one graph instance
The view abstracts rule implementation details and platform-specific execution failures

mathematical_views.question: Under which declared inputs and execution properties can an action result be reused without re-execution?
assumptions: An action key includes the inputs and relevant command or toolchain properties required by the cache contract
Sandboxing sufficiently constrains undeclared filesystem and process inputs for the modeled action
The relation is a candidate architectural view and does not prove that every action is hermetic

benefits: Explicit graph structure enables parallel and inspectable build planning
costs: Analysis and configuration complexity grows with rule and platform variation

benefits: Controlled inputs improve reproducibility across execution hosts
costs: Isolation constraints can expose undeclared dependencies and slow setup

benefits: Repeated work can be reused locally or through a shared remote cache
costs: Cache keys, invalidation, and remote service reliability require discipline
